title: Jeremiah’s alphabetic laments in four cycles
english: Jeremiah, the people having been taken captive and being in Babylon, laments the city and the country and the people for what has befallen them; and he laments marking off certain sections and divisions that begin next from the letters among the Hebrews. And after finishing the lament upon each letter and, upon all, the one that begins from Thau—which is the last letter of the Hebrews—he returns to Aleph and again laments; and he does this four times, going through the twenty-two letters.
translator_notes: GCS Orig. III Lam. fr. 1 lock.

title: Captivity of the contemplative soul; Christ frees captives
english: If we see the soul becoming subject to the devil or also to his angels, and simply to the hostile powers—the soul that by nature is contemplative and able to see the things that are and to attend—we will somehow understand the captivity and the one who took captive. But fleeing for refuge to Christ, who according to the prophet Isaiah proclaimed “release to captives,” we will be freed from the captivity, even if the one who took captive reaches as far as binding. For Jesus came “to lead out those bound from bonds and those sitting in darkness from a house of prison.”

title: Twenty-two books; fourfold alphabet; Symmachus and the Seventy
english: For this reason the Hebrews say the books of the old scripture are equal in number to the letters, so as to be every introduction toward knowledge of God, just as the letters are toward every wisdom for those learning. And for this reason it is quadrupled, perhaps because the elements of bodies also stand as four. And after a little: And the edition of Aquila and Theodotion is not extant in the Lamentations, but only of Symmachus and the Seventy. And again: And someone might inquire how, the title of the book being plural—“Lamentations”—he speaks this lament in the singular in the prologue. But there are several partial ones, divided by the letters, yet all are brought up into one, being brought up toward one subject, Israel.
translator_notes: GCS Orig. III Lam. fr. 3 lock.

title: People and nations: literal and anagogical
english: And the multitude of the people, as far as the wording, seems to indicate the dwelling Israelites, and the multitude of the nations, as we said before, the proselytes. But unto anagogy—since the contemplative things are more kindred to the soul and less circumstantial than the practical—the wealth of contemplations; and the multitude of the nations the large number of good deeds. And after a little: She who was multiplied with people sits alone; by casting off the bridegroom Word the bride becomes as a widow who once was filled with the aforementioned nations.

title: Jerusalem widowed of the Word; the perfect soul
english: As far as the wording it fits for Jerusalem to be understood as said with amazement because of the change unto the gloomier—sitting isolated who once was full of people—so that the isolation may be her desolation, having had as husband the living Word as protector when she followed him present and helping, but widowed and left behind by him because of the things she had sinned. And after other things: These things then toward the literal; toward the sense, Jerusalem flourishing and full of people and nations and ruling countries is the divine soul. And it is not amazing if not only a house nor a farmstead nor the village greater than this being named, nor an ordinary city, but one differing from all cities and honored beside God, is called Jerusalem—the perfect soul—greatness of notable size being thrown around her as around the greatest city by wisdom and every virtue multiplying buildings. And after a little: And just as it is possible to see Jerusalem flourishing, multiplying with people and nations and ruling in countries, so—if virtue is liable to fall—sometimes seeing her isolated and widowed and enslaved, so as even to pay tributes to the enemy who has mastered her, according to the soul of the one who has fallen from the truth.

title: Tribute to Nebuchadnezzar and his satraps
english: And what need is there also to speak concerning this—that having begun to rule countries she is enslaved to such a degree among the enemies that she always also pays tribute, doing whatever those masters command? And they command nothing useful. And perhaps for each of the things in which she stumbles here she pays some tribute to Nebuchadnezzar, who is interpreted “Settling-in and recognition of constraint”; and not only to Nebuchadnezzar, but also to his satraps.

title: She wept in the night; no comforter from those who loved her
english: Upon the first lament, the one that began from Aleph, we were able to save the wording. But upon this one what would someone say—a city being said to have wept in the night, so that the tears are upon her cheeks—unless perhaps someone will say that those named a city, who also pay tribute, have wept, having been reminded from what sort of peace and freedom into how great a slavery and humiliation they have come? How then shall we also narrate “in the night,” or that in the time of the common rest of all human beings the city, being reminded, while resting wept, and wept with the tears flowing fountain-like upon their cheeks? And the wailing was most stretched out for them and the tears flowed on, there not being even one comforting them from so many who loved them, and everyone who loved setting aside the friendship toward her and having changed into enmity. Who then, as toward the wording, are those who formerly loved her, from whom there was not one who would comfort her? Perhaps the remaining cities of Judea—loving the metropolis for this reason—in a time of distress did not encourage her.

And after a little: These things then toward the literal. If the Word, as in the things before, should be said to weep—having fallen from her own country and coming to be in Confusion—and to have a condition opposite to laughing the laugh from joy and cheerfulness, which our Lord promises will belong to those who have wept the blessed weeping, saying: “Blessed are those who weep now, for they will laugh.” And in Job also he says, “He will fill the mouth of the true ones with laughter.” And perhaps for this reason also one of the patriarchs is called Laughter. The one groaning, then—as also the apostle has made clear saying, “For indeed we who are in the tent groan, being burdened”—weeps a weeping most nourishing and benefiting the soul, toward the cheerfulness in promise.
translator_notes: GCS Orig. III Lam. fr. 10 lock.

title: Loving vs liking; better ones fail only to comfort
english: And we suppose that loving is more divine and, so to speak, spiritual, while liking is bodily and more human. And perhaps—since no base person loves—one must observe that concerning the better ones it says: “there is none comforting her from all who love her,” but concerning the lesser: “all who like her have set her aside; they have become enemies to her.” For the more deficient both set her aside and became enemies to her; but the better ones only did not comfort.

title: Judah exchanged her place through humiliation and slavery to passions
english: Toward the wording the sense would be such: Judea exchanged her own place, these things having become causes for her—her humiliation (in which she was humbled when she sinned and left behind the stature and the raised-up condition she formerly had while remaining in piety), and further also her much slavery, to which she had been enslaved when subjected to the passions. And having been relocated she settled among nations, where she has not been able to find rest, all the enemies pursuing her and overtaking and mastering her, she having come to be among the nations that were afflicting her.

title: Zion’s roads mourn; gates gone; priests and virgins led away
english: The sense toward the wording is this. The law saying, “Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear before the Lord your God,” those from the people were eager, after the temple was built in Zion from Solomon’s time, to accomplish what was commanded. And the cities of Judea being round about Jerusalem, from everywhere there were roads leading upon Zion. These roads, then, the prophet says mourn because of the captivity—looking gloomy and being in complete desolation—and in those times when there was much gladness and cheerfulness in them, when the Jews from everywhere were hastening unto a feast upon the mountain of Zion. And many being the gates built in Zion from all the quarters, the word says all have been made to vanish, and the priests unable to accomplish the other days—either because they have been taken captive or because there is no one approaching them and requiring the priestly liturgies. But also the virgins of Zion, it says, are being led away—clearly by the conquering enemies.
translator_notes: GCS Orig. III Lam. fr. 13 lock.

title: Roads of doctrines mourn when the contemplative power is captive
english: And toward the sense: Zion being called the looking-out and contemplative power, there are many roads of the varied doctrines—mystical and physical and ethical, and perhaps also logical—that lead upon the understanding and vision of the things set forth. Whenever, then, someone, having lost the practiced habit of these, is thrown into confusion, all these roads mourn, not being traveled—there being a festival for the aforementioned roads when they are traveled, examined and, so to speak, crossed through; but they mourn when they are desolated, not being researched nor journeyed through because those traveling have fallen away and, having been taken captive by the passions, have been distracted about the worse things.

title: Afflictors become head after sins against the prophets
english: The clarity of the wording is somehow such. Certain ones were afflicting the Judean country—or at least wanted to afflict—before the times of the captivity, but they did not master while God was shielding the Jews, when those were rendering themselves worthy of help. But when they sinned and, in addition to not hearing the prophets, the sons of Israel were even killing them, then they were handed over subject to the afflictors, so that their enemies became head—that is, as Symmachus interpreted, rulers. And others, perhaps besides the afflictors, being enemies either in conception or also in substance, were in prosperity, those abandoned because of the sins having become subject to the afflictors—the Lord having humbled the lawbreakers because of the multitude of the impieties, and having done this to such a degree that not even for their infants was mercy left, but that they went in captivity, driven by every afflictor.

title: Daughter Zion’s beauty gone; rulers like rams without pasture
english: The things of the wording, as far as power is ours, must be clarified, as we examine who the daughter of Zion is, and in what she has the comeliness, and what the pasture is which the rulers of the daughter of Zion do not have—like rams at a loss for grazing—and how these, deprived of strength, walk before the face of the pursuer. And we hold that the mountain Zion is mother of the synagogue in it, the synagogue being named daughter of Zion; and the comeliness of the daughter of Zion the possession in her robes, which possession, taken by the enemies in the time of the plundering, went out from those of whom it was adornment—that is, was carried out (for more emphatically he named this with “went out”); and the leaders of the synagogue, because the enemies were pressing and taking captive, being at a loss for the customary things, have been likened to rams not finding food. Just as rams driven without having been fed walk weakly, yielding to the necessity of those pursuing, so also the rulers, having become captives, being led away into the country of those who took them captive, were walking not in strength before the sight of the pursuer.

title: Contemplative soul as daughter of Zion; beauty of true doctrines
english: And toward the sense, such a soul is daughter of Zion: just as the just woman is daughter of righteousness and the wise woman child of wisdom, so—since Zion is the Lookout—the looking-out and theoretically traversing soul would be called daughter of Zion. And what else would I rightly suppose her comeliness and dignity to be than the wealth of the holy doctrines of the truth contemplated with wisdom? Whenever, then, after acquiring comeliness and dignity, someone neglects both the holding-together of these and the increase of the divine wealth, the things that until then were her adornment flow away and go out. And rulers—those who led the word and guided unto the acquisition of the aforementioned comeliness—like rams that led the flock of sheep and do not find pasture, have themselves also stood in scarcity, having let go the attention of the things able to fatten, so to speak, both them and the sheep. For this reason, having grown weak, having been overtaken by the pursuer—who is our adversary the devil—they walk before him, driven wherever that one wishes to lead. If, however, the aforementioned daughter of Zion takes care of her beauty and her comeliness and foresight that the dignity be guarded, she despises and sneers at the king of the Assyrians, as we have learned from Isaiah saying: “The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and sneered at you.”

title: Jerusalem remembers past humiliation when doctrines fall
english: For the one remembering while suffering such-and-such things does not remember the present, but the past. And after a little: Having raised such difficulties in the place and seeking a reminder of her past humiliation and of her rejections—because her people have fallen into a hand of an afflictor and the things brought upon her have come about—we consider whether perhaps humiliation in the proper sense is nothing other than sin, just as exaltation is right practice, and rejection comes about from nothing operating except base action; for this is sufficient to thrust away from God and from everything finest according to nature. When, then, Jerusalem was drunk—that is, those dwelling in her—and beside herself from the sin she was being humbled, she was not delighted in the stumbles; but when her repayments have come through her people having fallen into hands of the afflictor, no one helping her, then she was reminded of the things because of which she was suffering, grasping those as causes both of her people’s having fallen and of her having been left helpless.

And after a little: And if such a soul is Jerusalem, it is worthwhile to seek her people, upon whose falling into a hand of an afflictor—because there is no helper—she herself remembers the days of her humiliation, and still also of her own rejections by which she was rejected, and besides also of her desirable things, as many as were from ancient days. And see whether the contemplations in the knowing soul are not the people of Jerusalem, which, because the soul has come to be in inattention and neglect, falls, being thrown down by every afflictor. For the doctrines of those neglecting flow away, being squeezed out by the sins that have gained room in the one neglecting the better things, in no way having the help from the Word.
translator_notes: GCS Orig. III Lam. fr. 20 lock.
